mainTopic: The keys in God's hand, and when to begin mentioning rain on סוכות: the views of רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע, רבי יהודה בן בתירה, and רבי עקיבא, and their sources.
overview: This amud finishes רבי יוחנן's list of three 'keys' that God keeps in His own hand: rain, childbirth, and תחיית המתים. The sages of ארץ ישראל add פרנסה, and the גמרא explains that רבי יוחנן counts it within rain. Next, the גמרא asks where רבי אליעזר learned that we start mentioning rain on the first day of סוכות: from לולב, which is done only by day, or from ניסוך המים, which can start at night. רבי אבהו answers that the source is לולב, and the גמרא quotes a ברייתא that ties the start date to taking or putting down the לולב. In that ברייתא, רבי יהושע objects that rain on סוכות is a curse. רבי אליעזר answers that we only mention rain as praise, just as we mention תחיית המתים all year. The גמרא defends רבי יהושע: rain, unlike תחיית המתים, is good only in its season. Finally, the גמרא explains רבי יהודה בן בתירה's second-day view, based on the extra letters מ-י-ם that hint at ניסוך המים. It also explains רבי עקיבא's sixth-day view, which builds on that same water hint.

steps.title: Finishing the verse for the key of childbirth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes the פסוק about רחל, which proves that the key of childbirth is in God's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...to her, and God opened her womb.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of a פסוק that started earlier. It proves that God Himself holds the key to childbirth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof rests on the word 'opened' (ויפתח). Something that is 'opened' implies a key, and the פסוק says God Himself did the opening. So the key to childbirth was not handed to any messenger.

keyTerms.meaning: Key (here meaning control kept in God's hand)

phrases.english: to her, and God opened her womb.
phrases.notes: End of בראשית ל:כב, about רחל. The פסוק began earlier.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלֶיהָ אֱלֹהִים וַיִּפְתַּח אֶת רַחְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proof-text earlier (the key of childbirth).
steps.raayaObject: The key of childbirth is in God's hand alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: בראשית ל:כב, 'and He opened her womb.'

steps.title: Source for the key of resurrection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that the key of תחיית המתים is in God's hand. It answers with a פסוק from יחזקאל about God opening graves.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know about the key of תחיית המתים? As it is written: 'And you shall know that I am ה׳, when I open your graves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third key on רבי יוחנן's list, תחיית המתים, together with its proof פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the proof uses the language of 'opening' (בפתחי). God Himself opens the graves, so the key to bringing the dead back to life stays with Him. This completes the list of three keys.

keyTerms.meaning: Bringing the dead back to life

phrases.english: The key of the resurrection of the dead, from where do we know it?
As it is written: 'And you shall know that I am ה׳'
'when I open your graves.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַפְתֵּחַ שֶׁל תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third key in the same list.
steps.raayaObject: The key of תחיית המתים is in God's hand alone.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל לז:יג, 'when I open your graves.'
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן's three keys are rain, childbirth, and תחיית המתים. Each is proven by a פסוק that uses the language of God 'opening.'

steps.title: The West adds a key of livelihood
steps.stepSummary: The sages of ארץ ישראל say there is also a key of פרנסה in God's hand, based on 'You open Your hand.'
steps.simpleTranslation: In the West (ארץ ישראל) they say: also the key of פרנסה is in God's hand, as it is written: 'You open Your hand, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: A different tradition, from ארץ ישראל, adds a fourth key to רבי יוחנן's list: livelihood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They use the same 'opening' method. 'פותח את ידך' means God opens His hand to feed every living thing, so פרנסה is also controlled directly by Him. This sets up the question of why רבי יוחנן did not count it.

keyTerms.meaning: In the West, meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)

phrases.english: In the West they say:
Also the key of livelihood (is in God's hand),
as it is written: 'You open Your hand, etc.'
phrases.notes: תהלים קמה:טז, '...and satisfy every living thing with favor.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an expanded version of the list of keys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to ארץ ישראל, פרנסה is also one of the keys that God keeps in His own hand.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן leave out livelihood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not count the key of פרנסה in his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what is the reason that he did not count this one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that רבי יוחנן's list does not include פרנסה, even though there is a good פסוק for it. It asks why. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a clear פסוק shows that God holds the key of פרנסה, a complete list should include it. The question presses on whether רבי יוחנן disagrees, or whether he had some other reason for leaving it out.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is the reason
that he does not count this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב לְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions רבי יוחנן's list in light of the West's addition.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי יוחנן's list of keys does not include פרנסה.

steps.title: Rain already includes livelihood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן would answer that rain is the same thing as פרנסה, so the key of פרנסה is already on his list.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: rain is פרנסה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן: he did count פרנסה, because the key of rain covers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All food and livelihood depend on rain. So the key of rain already is the key of פרנסה. רבי יוחנן does not disagree with ארץ ישראל. He simply counts the two as one key.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
Rain is the same as livelihood.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: גְּשָׁמִים הַיְינוּ פַּרְנָסָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Rain and פרנסה are one key, since livelihood depends on rain.
steps.whatToRemember: There is no real argument here. ארץ ישראל lists פרנסה separately, and רבי יוחנן includes it within rain.

steps.title: Quoting רבי אליעזר's opinion in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה and quotes רבי אליעזר: rain is mentioned from the first יום טוב of סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: from the first יום טוב of the festival (סוכות), etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes רבי אליעזר's opinion. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי אליעזר says we start mentioning rain (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם) on the first day of סוכות. His wording does not make clear whether that means the night or the daytime. The next steps work on exactly that point.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc. (the rest of the משנה quote)

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:

phrases.aramaic: מִיּוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: From the first festival day of the Festival, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִיּוֹם טוֹב הָרִאשׁוֹן שֶׁל חַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the discussion of the keys has ended, and the גמרא goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, the mention of rain begins on the first day of סוכות.

steps.title: Where did רבי אליעזר learn this from?
steps.stepSummary: An איבעיא is raised: did רבי אליעזר learn his rule from the מצוה of לולב, or from ניסוך המים?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: from where did רבי אליעזר learn this? Did he learn it from לולב, or did he learn it from the water libation?
steps.whatsHappening: The sages raise a real question (איבעיא) about the source of רבי אליעזר's rule. They offer two possibilities, both מצוות of סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both לולב and ניסוך המים are connected to the rains of the coming year. So either one could be the model for when to start mentioning rain. Which model he used will decide the details of his rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked among them (a real, open question)
From where did he learn it?
Pouring water on the מזבח on סוכות

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
From where did Rabbi Eliezer learn this?
Did he learn it from the lulav,
or did he learn it from the water libation?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר מֵהֵיכָא גָּמַיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה's rule quoted in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי אליעזר's source is לולב or ניסוך המים.

steps.title: If from the lulav: start mentioning rain by day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the first side of the question. If the model is לולב, which is taken only by day, then הזכרה also begins only by day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he learned it from לולב, then just as לולב is in the daytime, so too הזכרה begins in the daytime.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out what the first option would mean in practice. This is still part of the question, not an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מצוה of לולב applies only during the day. If הזכרה copies לולב, the first mention of rain would come in the daytime תפילה of the first day of סוכות, not at מעריב the night before.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the conclusion. The גמרא is only laying out both sides of the question. Neither side has been decided yet.

phrases.english: If he learned it from the lulav:
just as the lulav is in the daytime,
so too the mention (of rain) is in the daytime.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִלּוּלָב גָּמַר לַהּ: מָה לוּלָב בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the practical result of the first side of the question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the mention of rain begins only in the daytime, as לולב does.

steps.title: If from the water libation: start mentioning rain from the night
steps.stepSummary: The second side: ניסוך המים can be done from the night, based on 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם.' If that is the model, הזכרה would begin at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps he learned it from ניסוך המים. Just as ניסוך המים can begin from the evening (as the Master taught, 'and their meal-offerings and their libations' means even at night), so too הזכרה begins from the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the second side of the question. It brings a source showing that ניסוך המים can begin at night, which would mean the mention of rain starts at night too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teaching of 'מר' reads 'ומנחתם ונסכיהם' to mean that certain מנחות and נסכים may be brought even at night. If הזכרה is modeled on ניסוך המים, it would begin at מעריב on the night of the first day of סוכות. So the practical difference between the two sides is night versus day.

keyTerms.meaning: As the Master said (quoting an earlier teaching)
And their meal-offerings and their libations (במדבר כט:יח)

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether, according to רבי אליעזר, the first mention of rain comes at מעריב on the night of סוכות or only in the daytime תפילה.
steps.whatToRemember: The question is lulav (only by day, so mention by day) versus ניסוך המים (possible from night, so mention from night).

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִנִּיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם גָּמַר לַהּ:
phrases.english: Or perhaps he learned it from the water libation:
just as the water libation is from the evening,
as the Master said: 'And their meal-offerings and their libations,'
phrases.notes: במדבר כט:יח, expounded to allow certain מנחות and נסכים at night.

phrases.english: (they may be brought) even at night,
so too the mention (of rain) is from the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ דִלְמָא מִנִּיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם גָּמַר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second side of the question, in contrast to step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the mention of rain begins from the night, as ניסוך המים does.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: The Source Is Lulav
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו resolves the איבעיא: רבי אליעזר learned his rule only from לולב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רבי אבהו said that רבי אליעזר learned this only from the לולב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Steps 7-9 by quoting רבי אבהו. He says the model is לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was whether רבי אליעזר's source was לולב (daytime only) or ניסוך המים (which can start at night). Since רבי אבהו says the source is לולב, הזכרה begins by day, just like לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; introduces a source that answers a question
He did not learn it (except from...)

steps.whyThisMatters: This settles the timing question. According to רבי אליעזר, we start mentioning rain in the daytime תפילה of the first day of סוכות, not at night.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rabbi Abbahu said:
Rabbi Eliezer did not learn it
except from the lulav.
phrases.notes: So הזכרה starts by day, like לולב.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the two-sided איבעיא laid out in Steps 7-9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אליעזר's source is לולב, so הזכרה begins by day.

steps.title: How רבי אבהו Knew This
steps.stepSummary: Two opinions on רבי אבהו's source: a received tradition, or a ברייתא he had heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רבי אבהו knew it as a tradition from his teachers. Others say he heard it from a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask how רבי אבהו knew where רבי אליעזר's rule came from. This sets up the quoting of the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the first view, רבי אבהו's statement is an oral tradition with no written source. According to the second view, he inferred it from a ברייתא. That second view leads the גמרא to bring the ברייתא next.

keyTerms.meaning: Some say; introduces an alternate version
He learned it as a received tradition
He heard it from a ברייתא

phrases.english: Some say:
Rabbi Abbahu learned it as a tradition,
and some say:
he heard it from a baraita.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ גְּמָרָא גְּמִיר לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the basis for רבי אבהו's statement in Step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אבהו's claim comes either from tradition or from a ברייתא.

steps.title: Which ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which ברייתא רבי אבהו heard.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is that ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short setup question. The גמרא is about to quote the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the second view says there is a ברייתא, we need to see it. Then we can understand how it shows that רבי אליעזר's source was לולב.

phrases.english: What is it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the ברייתא mentioned in the second view of Step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The text of the ברייתא behind רבי אבהו's statement.

steps.title: The ברייתא: From Taking the Lulav or From Putting It Down
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says we mention rain from when the לולב is taken. רבי יהושע says from when it is put down.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a ברייתא: From when do we mention rain? רבי אליעזר says: from when the לולב is taken. רבי יהושע says: from when it is put down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא. Both תנאים use the לולב to mark the time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ties the start of הזכרה to taking the לולב on the first day of סוכות. That is daytime, which is why רבי אבהו could say the source is לולב. רבי יהושע ties it to putting the לולב down, which means the end of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
Putting it down (at the end of סוכות)

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
From when do we mention the rains?

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: מִשְּׁעַת נְטִילַת לוּלָב.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: From the time of taking the lulav.
Rabbi Yehoshua says: From the time of putting it down.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: מֵאֵימָתַי מַזְכִּירִין עַל הַגְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא requested in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא uses the time of taking the לולב as רבי אליעזר's starting point.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's Reason: The Four Species Are About Water
steps.stepSummary: The ארבעה מינים come to ask for favor regarding water. Just as they cannot live without water, the world cannot live without water.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: These ארבעה מינים come only to seek favor for water. Just as they cannot exist without water, the world cannot exist without water.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי אליעזר's reason for linking rain to the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארבעה מינים are plants that need a lot of water, so they symbolize our need for rain. Because taking them is a prayer about water, it is the right moment to begin mentioning rain.

keyTerms.meaning: The ארבעה מינים: לולב, אתרוג, הדס, ערבה
To seek God's favor regarding water

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said:
Since these four species

phrases.aramaic: אֵינָן בָּאִין אֶלָּא לְרַצּוֹת עַל הַמַּיִם,
phrases.english: come only to seek favor for water,
and just as these four species
cannot exist without water,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ אִי אֶפְשָׁר לָעוֹלָם בְּלֹא מַיִם.
phrases.english: so too the world cannot exist without water.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: הוֹאִיל וְאַרְבַּעַת מִינִין הַלָּלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רבי אליעזר's position from Step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Taking the ארבעה מינים is a plea about water, so הזכרת גשמים begins when they are taken.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: Rain on Sukkot Is a Curse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע objects: rain during סוכות is a sign of a curse, so why mention it then?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: But rain on the חג is only a sign of a curse!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain on סוכות forces people out of the סוכה, so it is a bad sign. רבי יהושע argues that bringing up rain during the חג makes no sense if we do not want it to fall then.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so that...?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:
But is not rain on the festival
nothing but a sign of a curse!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא גְּשָׁמִים בֶּחָג אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא סִימָן קְלָלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אליעזר's reasoning from Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's rule that we mention rain from the first day of סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Rain during סוכות is unwanted, so speaking about it during the חג seems wrong.

steps.title: Mentioning Is Not Asking: The Comparison to Resurrection
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר answers that he only meant mentioning rain, not asking for it. Like תחיית המתים, we can praise God's power all year even though it happens only at its proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: I too did not say to ask for rain, only to mention it. Just as we mention תחיית המתים all year, though it will come only at its time, so we mention the power of rain all year, though rain falls only in its season. Therefore, if a person wants to mention rain all year, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר defends his view by separating praising God's power to bring rain from requesting that rain fall now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הזכרה (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם) is praise, not a request. Praising God's power does not mean we want rain right now, just as mentioning תחיית המתים does not mean we expect it today. So the objection falls away, and רבי אליעזר even allows mentioning rain all year.

keyTerms.meaning: To ask, i.e., request rain (ותן טל ומטר)
To mention, i.e., praise God's power (משיב הרוח)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up לשאול and להזכיר. Asking (ותן טל ומטר in ברכת השנים) is a request for rain now. Mentioning (משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם in the second ברכה) is only praise. רבי אליעזר's whole answer depends on this difference.
steps.whatToRemember: הזכרה is praise of God's power, not a request. That is why it can be said even when we do not want rain to fall.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him:
I too did not say to ask,
but only to mention.
And just as the resurrection of the dead
one mentions the entire year,
yet it comes only in its time,
so too we mention the might of the rains
all year,
yet they come only in their season.
Therefore, if one comes to mention
the entire year, he may mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף אֲנִי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי לִשְׁאוֹל, אֶלָּא לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי יהושע's challenge from Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning rain on סוכות seems to be a request for rain, which would be a curse.
steps.terutzMaskana: הזכרה is only praise of God's power, like mentioning תחיית המתים all year, so it is allowed even all year.

steps.title: רבי: Stop Mentioning When You Stop Asking
steps.stepSummary: רבי holds that once a person stops asking for rain, he also stops mentioning it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: I say that from the time one stops asking for rain, one also stops mentioning it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with a third view, from רבי, which limits רבי אליעזר's idea of mentioning rain all year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר allowed mentioning rain all year because it is only praise. רבי disagrees: הזכרה is tied to שאלה, so when the request for rain ends, the mention of rain ends too.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא, editor of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views in the ברייתא. רבי אליעזר: start from taking the לולב, and one may mention all year. רבי יהושע: start from putting the לולב down. רבי: mention and request stop together.

phrases.english: Rebbi says: I say:
from the time one stops asking,
so too one stops mentioning.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אוֹמֵר, אוֹמֵר אֲנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the end of Step 16, where רבי אליעזר allows mentioning rain all year.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הזכרה ends when שאלה ends; one may not mention rain all year.

steps.title: More opinions: the second day or the sixth day of סוכות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יהודה בן בתירה says we start mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. רבי עקיבא says we start on the sixth day.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: On the second day of the festival, one mentions rain. רבי עקיבא says: On the sixth day of the festival, one mentions rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds two more opinions about when we begin mentioning rain during סוכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we had רבי אליעזר (from when the לולב is taken, at the start of סוכות) and רבי יהושע (from when it is put down, at the end of סוכות). Now two middle opinions are added: the second day and the sixth day. The גמרא will soon explain where the second-day opinion comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: On the second day of the festival (סוכות)
On the sixth day of the festival (סוכות)
He mentions, meaning he says 'משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם'

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
On the second day of the festival, one mentions rain,
Rabbi Akiva says:
On the sixth day of the festival, one mentions rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר: בַּשֵּׁנִי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of opinions in the ברייתא after רבי's view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: start mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. רבי עקיבא: start on the sixth day.

steps.title: Which prayer leader starts and which stops mentioning rain
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה, quoting רבי יהושע, explains the exact switch. On שמיני עצרת, the second חזן (מוסף) starts mentioning rain and the first (שחרית) does not. On the first day of פסח it is the opposite: the first חזן still mentions rain, and the second stops.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יהושע: The one who leads the prayers on the last יום טוב of סוכות: the last leader mentions rain, and the first leader does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח: the first leader mentions rain, and the last leader does not.
steps.whatsHappening: This opinion explains exactly at which תפילה the switch to and from mentioning rain happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שמיני עצרת, שחרית still has no mention of rain, and from מוסף on we mention it. On the first day of פסח the opposite happens: שחרית still mentions rain, and from מוסף we stop. This follows רבי יהושע's view that we start mentioning rain only at the end of סוכות.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark: the prayer leader (חזן)
The last יום טוב of סוכות, which is שמיני עצרת
The first leader (שחרית) and the last leader (מוסף)

steps.confusionAlert: 'הראשון' and 'האחרון' here mean the first and last prayer leader on that day (שחרית and מוסף). They do not mean the first and last days of the festival.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
The one who passes before the ark (prayer leader)
on the last Festival day of the festival (שמיני עצרת):
the last one (מוסף) mentions rain,
phrases.notes: From מוסף onward, rain is mentioned.

phrases.english: the first one (שחרית) does not mention rain.
On the first Festival day of Passover:
the first one mentions rain,
the last one does not mention rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further opinion that gives the exact practical details of the switch.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שמיני עצרת, mentioning rain begins at מוסף. On the first day of פסח, mentioning rain stops at מוסף.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר's argument seems very strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא remarks that רבי אליעזר answered רבי יהושע well. If we mention תחיית המתים all year, why not rain? So how can רבי יהושע disagree?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר spoke well to רבי יהושע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the debate in steps 15-16. It says רבי אליעזר's answer looks so convincing that רבי יהושע's view seems hard to defend.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר argued that mentioning rain is only praise, just like praising תחיית המתים every day. The גמרא is asking: what could רבי יהושע possibly say back to this? This challenge sets up the defense in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He spoke well to him, meaning his argument is strong

phrases.english: He is speaking well to him:
Rabbi Eliezer to Rabbi Yehoshua!

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע exchange and puts pressure on רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's view that we should not mention rain during סוכות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If praising God's power over תחיית המתים is fine all year, praising His power over rain should be fine during סוכות too.

steps.title: Rain is different from תחיית המתים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע could answer: any day is a proper time for תחיית המתים, so we can mention it any day. But rain is not good at every time it falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע would say to you: It makes sense that we mention תחיית המתים every day, because every day is a proper time for it. But rain: is every time it comes its proper time?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יהושע by showing a difference between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תחיית המתים would be welcome on any day, so praising it daily fits. Rain, however, has a proper season, and outside that season it is not a blessing. So mentioning rain when it is not wanted, such as during סוכות, does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: He would say to you: introduces a possible answer for someone
It makes sense / granted (the first part of a contrast)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua would say to you:
Granted, resurrection of the dead one mentions,
because every day is its proper time.
But rain,
is every time it comes its proper time?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְךָ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ: בִּשְׁלָמָא תְּחִיַּית הַמֵּתִים מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 for רבי יהושע.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Mentioning rain is just like mentioning תחיית המתים: pure praise that fits any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: תחיית המתים is welcome on any day, but rain is welcome only in its season. So praise of rain belongs only in its season.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that mentioning rain is tied to its proper season, which is why the timing debate exists at all.

steps.title: Proof: rain at the wrong time is a curse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: if rain falls after ניסן is over, it is a sign of a curse, as the פסוק says about rain during the wheat harvest.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: If ניסן has passed and rain falls, it is a sign of a curse, as it says: 'Is it not the wheat harvest today...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the answer in step 21 with a משנה showing that rain outside its season is harmful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה proves that rain is not good at every time. After ניסן, rain hurts the harvest. In שמואל א', rain during the wheat harvest was brought as a sign of God's anger. This backs רבי יהושע's point that rain has a proper time.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה: introduces a source

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's position: we mention rain only when rain is a blessing. Since rain during סוכות (and after ניסן) is a curse, we wait until the end of סוכות.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a mishna:
If Nisan has ended and rains fall,
they are a sign of a curse,
as it is stated: "Is it not the wheat harvest today, etc."
phrases.notes: שמואל א' יב:יז. Rain at harvest time was a sign of God's displeasure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן: יָצָא נִיסָן וְיָרְדוּ גְּשָׁמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the claim in step 21 that rain is not always in its proper time.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that rain is not welcome at every time
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה (תענית יב:) that rain after ניסן is a sign of a curse, based on שמואל א' יב:יז

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reason?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה בן בתירה's opinion (start on the second day of סוכות) and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says: On the second day of the festival one mentions rain. What is the reason of רבי יהודה בן בתירה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It re-quotes רבי יהודה בן בתירה's opinion from the ברייתא and asks why he picked the second day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting on the first or last day is easy to understand, but the second day seems random. The גמרא wants the source that singles out the second day of סוכות.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
On the second day of the festival, one mentions rain.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה?
phrases.english: What is the reason of Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע debate and opens a new question about the opinion in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for starting to mention rain on the second day of סוכות

steps.title: Introducing a ברייתא as the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a ברייתא in which רבי יהודה בן בתירה speaks. Its content follows in steps 25-26.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה בן בתירה says:
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a setup. The גמרא is starting to bring the ברייתא that will explain רבי יהודה בן בתירה's reason, and the actual words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source will be a hint in the תורה to the water libation (ניסוך המים) on סוכות. It comes from small changes in wording, and the first one appears on the second day. As step 28 explains, that is why רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts mentioning rain on the second day.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
The water libation poured on the מזבח during סוכות (the topic of the coming ברייתא)

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ברייתא where רבי יהודה בן בתירה derives the water libation from a hint in the תורה's description of the סוכות offerings, which begins on the second day (spelled out in steps 25-26).

steps.title: Three unusual plural words in the סוכות offerings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירה points out three words in the קרבנות of סוכות that are written in an unusual plural form: on day two, day six, and day seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says on the second day 'ונסכיהם' (their libations), it says on the sixth day 'ונסכיה' (its libations), and it says on the seventh day 'כמשפטם' (according to their laws).
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and lists three words from the פסוקים about the סוכות offerings that are spelled differently from the other days. This sets up the next line, where those differences will spell out a word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the other days of סוכות, the תורה uses singular forms like ונסכה and כמשפט. On these three days, the words have an extra letter: a מ in ונסכיהם, a י in ונסכיה, and a מ in כמשפטם. These extra letters are the raw material for a hidden hint.

keyTerms.meaning: And their libations (plural, with an extra מ). Said on day two
And its libations (plural, with an extra י). Said on day six
According to their laws (with an extra מ). Said on day seven

steps.confusionAlert: The point is NOT the meaning of these words. The point is that each one has an 'extra' letter compared to how the תורה writes the same idea on the other days. Only the extra letters count.

phrases.english: It is said on the second day: 'and their libations'
phrases.notes: Extra letter: מ (other days say ונסכה).

phrases.english: and it is said on the sixth day: 'and its libations'
and it is said on the seventh day: 'according to their laws'
phrases.notes: Extra letter: מ (other days say כמשפט).

steps.triggerLanguage: נֶאֱמַר בַּשֵּׁנִי ״וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא introduced in Step 24, giving the textual basis for רבי יהודה בן בתירה's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source starts from three unusual plural words in the סוכות offering פסוקים.

steps.title: The extra letters spell 'water', a hint to the water-pouring
steps.stepSummary: The extra letters מ, י, מ together spell מים (water). This is a hint in the תורה to ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here you have מ, י, מ. Here you have מים (water). From here comes a hint to the water-pouring from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא puts the three extra letters together and shows that they spell 'water'. This finishes the derivation: the תורה hints at ניסוך המים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 25 collected three extra letters. Here they are combined, in order, into the word מים. Since this is only a רמז (hint) and not a clear command, the ברייתא is careful to call it a 'hint' from the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The water-pouring on the מזבח during סוכות

steps.whyThisMatters: ניסוך המים on סוכות is tied to the world being judged for rain at that time. So once we know which day the תורה hints at the water-pouring, we know which day to start mentioning rain.

phrases.english: Here is mem, yod, mem
phrases.notes: The three extra letters, in order of the days.

phrases.english: here you have 'water' (mayim)

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן רֶמֶז לְנִיסּוּךְ הַמַּיִם מִן הַתּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: from here is a hint to the water libation from the Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי מֵ״ם יוֹ״ד מֵ״ם, הֲרֵי כָּאן מַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Combines the letters gathered in Step 25 into the word מים and draws the conclusion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תורה contains a hint to ניסוך המים through the letters מ-י-ם found on days two, six, and seven of סוכות.

steps.title: Why start on the second day?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה בן בתירה chose the second day of סוכות to start mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is different about the second day, that he chose it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question. The hint is spread over three days, so why does רבי יהודה בן בתירה pick day two in particular? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hint מים uses letters from days two, six, and seven. So it is not obvious why the second day, and not the sixth or seventh, should be the starting point.

phrases.english: And what is different about the second day that he chose it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא בְּשֵׁנִי דְּנָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the hint derived in Step 26 leads specifically to the second day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the second day is chosen when the hint is spread over three days.

steps.title: The hint first appears on the second day
steps.stepSummary: The hint to water first shows up on the second day, so that is where we begin mentioning rain.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because when the פסוק hints at them, it is on the second day that it first hints. Therefore, on the second day we mention rain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The first letter of the hint, the מ in ונסכיהם, appears on day two, so that is the starting point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hint begins on day two, even though it is only completed on day seven. רבי יהודה בן בתירה goes by where the hint starts. So the mention of rain starts on the second day.

phrases.english: Because when the verse hints at them,
it is on the second day that it hints at them;
therefore, on the second day we mention rain.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּכִי רְמִיזִי לְהוּ בִּקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hint first begins on the second day, so mentioning rain starts then.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה בן בתירה: the extra letters מ-י-ם on days 2, 6, and 7 hint at ניסוך המים. We start mentioning rain on day 2, where the hint begins.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: start on the sixth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says we start mentioning rain on the sixth day of סוכות. The plural word ונסכיה on that day hints at two pourings: water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: On the sixth day of the festival he mentions rain, as it says on the sixth day 'ונסכיה' (its libations). The פסוק is speaking of two libations: one is the water libation and one is the wine libation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives רבי עקיבא's view, with its own source. He reads the single word ונסכיה on day six as a hint to two pourings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא looks at day six, where the plural 'libations' means two pourings. He reads them as one water pouring and one wine pouring, so rain is mentioned starting from the sixth day. The next step asks how he knows the extra pouring is water. Step 31 answers that he relies on רבי יהודה בן בתירה's water hint.

keyTerms.meaning: The wine libation (the regular pouring with every קרבן)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי עקיבא uses the same word, ונסכיה, as רבי יהודה בן בתירה, but in a different way. For רבי יהודה בן בתירה it supplies one letter (י). For רבי עקיבא the plural itself means 'two pourings'.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
On the sixth day of the festival one mentions rain,
as it is said on the sixth day: 'and its libations';
the verse is speaking of two libations:
one is the water libation,
and one is the wine libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: בַּשִּׁשִּׁי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a competing opinion in the same ברייתא, with a different reading of the same type of hint.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Rain is mentioned starting on the sixth day of סוכות, because ונסכיה hints at both a water and a wine libation.

steps.title: Maybe both pourings are wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא: the plural ונסכיה could mean two wine pourings, not water and wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both of them are of wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבי עקיבא. Fine, the plural word hints at two pourings, but why say one of them is water? Maybe both are wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's proof depended on the plural form of ונסכיה meaning two pourings. The challenge accepts that there are two pourings. It only attacks the claim that one of them is water, since a plural word alone does not say what is being poured.

keyTerms.meaning: Say / one could say (introduces another possible reading)

phrases.english: Say that both of them are of wine!
phrases.notes: The 'both' refers to the two pourings hinted at by the plural ונסכיה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ דְּחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's reading of ונסכיה from Step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that the two pourings in ונסכיה are water and wine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A plural word shows there are two pourings, but it does not show that one is water. Both could be wine.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא relies on the water hint of רבי יהודה בן בתירה
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי יהודה בן בתירה that these extra letters hint to water, so the second pouring is water.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds like רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who said: water is hinted at here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי יהודה בן בתירה that the extra letters in these words hint at water. So the extra pouring must be water and not more wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא does not reject רבי יהודה בן בתירה's idea. He takes it as a starting point: the extra letters are about water. Where the two of them differ is only which day the hint begins. For רבי עקיבא, it is the sixth day, through ונסכיה.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds like / agrees with the view of

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone here agrees that the extra letters hint to water. רבי עקיבא only argues about the starting day. For him it is the sixth day, because the plural ונסכיה shows two pourings: water and wine.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי יהודה בן בתירה about the water hint. He accepts it. They only argue about which day it starts.

phrases.aramaic: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה,
phrases.english: He holds in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
who said: water is alluded to.
phrases.notes: Refers back to Steps 25 and 26, where the extra letters spelled מים.

steps.triggerLanguage: סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Draws on another תנא's source: the water hint of רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two pourings hinted at in ונסכיה could both be wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since these extra letters are about water, the second pouring is water. So ונסכיה hints at water and wine.
